title: How to apply partner developer account
Institutional Crypto Buy/Sell Solution — Integration Guideline
snippet:
> This guideline helps partners (merchants) integrate Institutional Crypto Buy/Sell Solution's Open API from scratch. Follow the steps below to go from zero to live.

- Most APIs require a `userId` parameter — this is the Binance sub-account ID obtained after completing user onboarding via [Binance Link KYC SaaS](https://developers.binance.com/en/docs/products/kyc-saas/overview). You must integrate Binance CaaS first before calling Institutional Crypto Buy/Sell Solution APIs.

### Items Binance Provides to You
| # | Item | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Client ID** | Your unique partner identifier (`X-Tesla-ClientId`) |
| 2 | **Sign Access Token** | Access token for API authentication (`X-Tesla-SignAccessToken`) |
| 3 | **Webhook Public Key** | Binance's public key for verifying webhook signatures |

title: Getting Started
snippet:
- Your **master account** must hold the CAAS permission. Every CAAS endpoint is called with the master account's API key; most of them sit under `/sapi/v1/broker/*`.

| Level | What it is |
|---|---|
| Master account | The partner's own Binance account. Holds the CAAS permission and is the parent of every end-user account. |
| Sub-account | One Binance account per end user, created by the partner through the API. Holds the end user's balances and orders. |
| Sub-account API key | The credential used to trade or transfer on a single sub-account's behalf. |
